A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StreamDiT work. All 16 pages of each version, including the supplementary material, are readable, and corresponding text, equations, tables and figures can be matched.

before.justification: v3 reports original VBench results, human evaluations, streaming demonstrations and ablations, including the supplementary 30B-model experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains the original quantitative evaluations, human evaluations, demonstrations and main-text and supplementary ablations.

M1.justification: Buffered flow matching, mixed partitioning, time-varying adaLN DiT, window attention and multistep distillation are retained. The new KV-cache discussion concerns future work, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training-video collections and Movie Gen evaluation prompts, with the same long-video, interactive-generation and video-to-video scenarios. The 30B demonstrations already appear in v3's appendix.

E2.justification: ReuseDiffuse and FIFO-Diffusion remain the evaluated comparators in Table 2 and Figure 5; the Progressive AR Diffusion configuration remains in the mixed-training ablation. Newly cited Self Forcing is not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: The shared-backbone comparisons, 50 evaluation prompts, VBench metrics, 8-second 512p human-evaluation videos, training budgets and inference configurations are unchanged. Learning-rate typesetting changes do not alter their values.

E4.justification: The mixed-chunk ablation in Table 3 and the reference-frame and T2V-mixing ablations in Table 4 are unchanged. The streaming, storytelling and editing case studies retain the same examples and analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-score and human-preference reporting. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, seed specifications, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 2–4, Figure 5, timing measurements and displayed video frames are unchanged. However, Section 6 removes the explicit observations of the cat's Janus artifact and the rally car's motion artifacts, replacing these concrete qualitative findings with a generic acknowledgment of artifacts.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the buffer enumeration from [f_i, ..., f_{i+B}] to [f_{i+1}, ..., f_{i+B}], making the listed length B rather than B+1. The other mathematical formulations, including the supplementary noise-scheduling definition, are retained.

C1.justification: The core contributions remain buffered streaming training, mixed partitioning, efficient DiT modeling and tailored distillation. Both versions claim 512p generation at 16 FPS on one GPU and support the same applications.

C2.justification: Section 6 foregrounds the context-length limitation already present in v3's appendix, adds an extended-window/KV-cache mitigation, and asserts that capacity and context limitations are not fundamental. It drops the earlier large-to-small-model distillation suggestion. The introduction also expands the attention-quality and latency rationale.

D1.justification: Architecture details, learning rates, iteration counts, hardware, inference-thread organization and the project-site link are retained. The added appendix pointer directs readers to existing training details rather than newly disclosed settings.

R1.justification: v4 adds Self Forcing and Autoregressive Image Generation without Vector Quantization, strengthening the discussion of autoregressive versus bidirectional generation. It removes the discussion and references for CogVideo, CogView2, Video Diffusion Models, Imagen Video and Lumiere, while retaining the broader positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, related-work passages and limitations paragraph receive localized rewrites. Section 2.2 becomes 'Extensible Video Generation,' and reference-frame terminology is refined. The overall section sequence and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 moves from PDF page 7 to page 6, text reflows, page-number footers disappear, and Figures 12 and 15 receive small caption edits. The figures and table structures otherwise remain the same.

improvement.justification: The buffer-index correction and updated positioning provide small clarity gains, while removing specific artifact observations reduces diagnostic detail. The revised conclusion makes an existing limitation more prominent but adds only a proposed remedy. With the methods, validation, reproducibility information and detailed appendix retained, overall paper quality remains broadly unchanged.
